docs.purpose: Powers a map view: given the rectangle of map currently on screen, it returns the permits inside it — optionally filtered by status, trade, or minimum project cost — plus a quick count and average cost for that view.
docs.data_story: It reads 3 tables — `permits`, `permit_trades` and `trades` and writes nothing. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 11 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: No SPEC LINK header anywhere in the file. No explicit auth/session check in the handler; public by route-guard classification. permit_trades/trades are joined only when a trade_slug filter is supplied; otherwise the query is against permits alone. No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: DISCLOSURE (unauthenticated): the projection is explicit (11 columns, route.ts:59-71) but includes `latitude`/`longitude` — the exact geocoded coordinates of every permit inside a caller-chosen bounding box — alongside `est_const_cost` (the construction valuation), the street address parts (street_num/street_name/street_type) and `ward`. No owner or builder name here. An anonymous caller can sweep the whole city by walking the bbox: up to 2,000 rows per call, no rate limit, no auth, and the second query hands back the exact viewport `total` and `avg_cost` (route.ts:80-86, :91-92) which leaks the population size beyond the returned page. avg_cost over a 1-row viewport is that permit's valuation. Second finding: `parseInt(minCost, 10)` at route.ts:43 has no NaN guard, so ?min_cost=abc binds NaN (node-postgres will send it as the string 'NaN' into a numeric comparison — a DB error, i.e. a 500, not a 400). CHECKLIST agreement: routes-index.json census_reads (permits, permit_trades, trades) matches exactly; permit_trades/trades are reached only when ?trade_slug is supplied (route.ts:48-53). | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic export and no Cache-Control header in src/app/api/permits/geo/route.ts:1-96 | Pagination: limit only, no offset: Math.min(parseInt(limit||'500',10), 2000) at route.ts:21, bound as the last $n (route.ts:75-76). Upper clamp only; no lower clamp and no NaN guard on parseInt. There is no cursor or page param, so the viewport `total` (route.ts:91) can exceed the returned rows with no way to fetch the remainder. | Other guards / classification: PUBLIC: '/api/permits' prefix (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:70) matched at route-guard.ts:170 -> 'public'; middleware pass-through src/middleware.ts:43-45 | ORPHAN — zero call sites in src/** or mobile/** (sweep 2026-09-15, comment lines stripped). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.
